title: Covering number IS subgroup distinct r-fold subset-sum, base-{2,3} bracket [2^{n/2},3^{n/2}] capped by p
evidence: Two exact probes in the PRIZE regime (n=2^mu PROPER subgroup, q==1 mod n, q~n^beta, beta in {4,5}; primitive n-th root g found, g^{n/2}=-1 verified). scripts/probes/_407_conn/C027_covering_fieldcap.py: char-0 full-subgroup distinct subset-sum count = 3^{n/2} EXACTLY (signed cube {-1,0,1}^{n/2} image, power-basis independent) and half-domain = 2^{n/2} -- confirms the in-tree PROVEN bracket [2^{n/2},3^{n/2}] (SubsetSumLowerLoop50.card_subsetSumset_isPrimitiveRoot_two_pow_ge ge 2^{2^{m-1}}; SubgroupSumsetThreePowUpper.subsetSumset_full_le_three_pow le 3^N; subsetSumset_full_le_min le min(3^N,p)). EXACT enumeration n=8 (3^4=81) and n=16 (3^8=6561) at q=4129/32801/65537/1048609: realized==3^half==min(3^half,q) since 3^half<q (cap NOT yet binding). scripts/probes/_407_conn/C027_saturation.py (DECISIVE): at n=32 (q=4129, 3^16=43046721>>q) and n=64 (q=17729, 3^32=1.85e15>>q) the realized distinct-subset-sum count = q EXACTLY (coverage cnt/q = 1.0000 both) -- the signed cube SURJECTS onto all of F_q. So once 3^{n/2}>=q (which for the real prize n=2^30, q~2^150 happens at half=2^29 >> log_3 q ~ 95, i.e. instantly) the realized covering/bad-count = min(3^{n/2},p) = p EXACTLY (field cap is the binding edge, saturated).
wall: BGK/Paley (W-largesieve cluster). The connection PROVES the covering/far-count is doubly-exponential combinatorially and field-capped at p (saturating p in-regime), but the count being p (or >> budget) is NOT the prize obstruction: the obstruction is whether those p candidate bad scalars are GENUINELY bad (line-explainable AND beyond the decoding radius), which is exactly the sub-sqrt(q) incomplete-character-sum / generalized-Paley-eigenvalue B=max_b||eta_b|| wall. The subset-sum COUNT (this connection's object) is blind to that cancellation question. The cited walls W-Mersenne/W-idealSVP are the upper-bracket (subgroup-sumset covering) side, not in play for the count-saturation conclusion here.
honest_note: Not a closure and the connection record itself never claimed one (why_insightful: 'only the field cap p keeps the prize alive'; the in-tree SubgroupSumsetThreePowUpper docstring: 'does NOT close the prize', 'prize survives sec7'). The PROVEN/PARTIAL half: the exact spectrum law N(mu,r)=sum_a 2^a C(n/2,a), the two-sided base-{2,3} bracket, the field cap, AND the new fact that the cap SATURATES (cube surjects onto F_q in-regime, cov=1.0000 at n=32,64) are all verified/in-tree-axiom-clean. The OPEN half (the prize core) is untouched: the count saturating p does not decide whether epsMCA exceeds the budget, because that needs the BGK/Paley sqrt-cancellation among the (q-1)/n Gauss-sum phases, a recognized 25-year-open problem. Reframing 'is the bad count <= budget' as 'does mod-p collapse the cube below n' is decidable and ANSWERED here (no: it saturates p >> n), which is precisely why the count cannot be the discriminator -- consistent with the field-cap framing being an honest delimiter, not a route to the prize. Probe caps: n=32/64 saturation used q~4n^2 small primes (so q is an enumerable coverage target); the real prize q is larger, making 3^{n/2}/q MORE extreme, so the cap binds even harder -- the conclusion strengthens, not weakens, at true prize scale. n=128 saturation case was dropped (primitive-root search timed out); n=32,64 already establish cov=1.0000 surjection.
